_source.tables: Table 7 Example Severity Classification (p.34), Table 8 Example Likelihood Classification (p.35), Table 9 Example Clinical Risk Matrix (p.35), Table 10 Example Risk Acceptability Definitions (p.37)

_note: The guidance labels all four tables 'Example' and says the classifications are illustrative: the Health Organisation decides its own in the Clinical Risk Management Plan (DCB0160 3.2.1, guidance 4.4). HAZLOG proposes a cell on this example matrix; it never confirms one. Severity definitions below summarise Table 7, which is organised by harm and by whether one or multiple patients are affected.

severity.definition: Minor injury from which recovery is expected in the short term; minor psychological upset; inconvenience; any negligible severity (single patient)

Minor injury from which recovery is not expected in the short term, or significant psychological trauma (single patient); minor injury with short-term recovery, or minor psychological upset or inconvenience (multiple patients)

Severe injury or severe incapacity from which recovery is expected in the short term, or severe psychological trauma (single patient); minor injury from which recovery is not expected in the short term, or significant psychological trauma (multiple patients)

Death, or permanent life-changing incapacity, or severe injury or incapacity from which recovery is not expected in the short term (single patient); severe injury or incapacity with short-term recovery, or severe psychological trauma (multiple patients)
Death, or permanent life-changing incapacity, or severe injury or incapacity from which recovery is not expected in the short term (multiple patients)

likelihood.definition: Negligible or nearly negligible possibility of occurring
Could occur but in the great majority of occasions will not
Not certain but very possible; reasonably expected to occur in the majority of cases
Certain or almost certain; highly likely to occur

acceptability.4: Mandatory elimination of hazards or addition of control measures to reduce risk to an acceptable level
acceptability.3: Undesirable level of risk. Attempts should be made to eliminate the hazards or implement control measures to reduce risk to an acceptable level. Shall only be acceptable when further risk reduction is impractical
acceptability.2: Acceptable where cost of further reduction outweighs benefits gained or where further risk reduction is impractical
